stories.title: Clasping folds enable superior elastic strength of graphene films
stories.description: Two-dimensional graphene sheets show strong potential for use in fabrication of macroscopic films, as they have exceptional mechanical properties owing to their in-plane strength1–6. Improvements in the stacking order of flat two-dimensional sheets have led to corresponding improvements in the strength and toughness of such films7–11. In addition, modulation of the spatial conformation of individual units has enabled the development of benchmark materials with superior properties12,13; however, this has remained elusive in the case of two-dimensional sheets. Here we report a strategy for preparation of graphene films with a combination of high strength (2.9 GPa), toughness (84.5 MJ m−3) and elastic strain (5%). We attribute these performance gains to a fold-clasping lamellar structure achieved by modular assembly of surface-folded multilayer graphene oxide flakes. We identify a pull-to-push transition of force chain topology and propose a shear-lock stress transfer strategy in the fold-clasping lamellar graphene film that enables advances in mechanical properties. This work demonstrates the modular design of spatial conformation of two-dimensional flakes on a large scale and further improves the performance of macroscopic films for potential applications in lightweight structural components. Two-dimensional graphene films with unusual folded surfaces are synthesized through a modular assembly strategy and show enhanced strength, toughness and elastic strain owing to stress distribution between interlayer folds.

stories.title: TMEM59 modulates TREM2-regulated microglial responses in ischemia and serves as a potential therapeutic target
stories.description: Microglial responses mediated by the triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) play a crucial role in ischemia, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Herein, we found that TREM2 and its interacting protein, transmembrane protein 59 (TMEM59), had opposite expression dynamics in microglia from mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) and HMC3 cells treated with oxygen–glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), with TREM2 expression gradually increased, whereas TMEM59 expression increased first and then gradually decreased after ischemia modeling. We confirmed that TREM2 deficiency deteriorated neurological function impairments, cell apoptosis, microgliosis, and neuroinflammation in MCAO/R mice. Notably, TMEM59 haploinsufficiency dramatically attenuated the exacerbated impairments in TREM2-deficient mice with MCAO/R. Mechanistically, TMEM59 deficiency suppressed aberrant autophagy activation and neuroinflammation in microglia following MCAO/R and OGD/R. Moreover, both microglia-specific and systemic deletion of TMEM59 ameliorated neurological function impairments, cell apoptosis, microgliosis, neuroinflammation, and aberrant autophagy in MCAO/R mice. Finally, we developed a peptide targeting TMEM59 to promote its degradation and showed that treatment with this peptide reduced TMEM59 protein levels and effectively rescued neurological impairments and related pathologies in MCAO/R mice. Our findings establish TMEM59 as a key negative regulator of TREM2 function in microglia and a key driver of maladaptive microglial autophagy and neuroinflammation in ischemia, indicating that TMEM59 reduction represents a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemia treatment.
